parsed.explanation: Combined operative regime: national passport sex-marker restrictions (Supreme Court allowed them in Nov 2025) and entry refusal guidance (discrepancy leads to refusal; lifetime fraud ineligibility possible) apply to every visitor. Immigration custody has documented forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men. The state's facilities statute makes trespass a criminal offence with documented handcuffing and 24 hours held in a men's ward; state troopers conducted ID checks at restrooms. The state has no gender-identity anti-discrimination statute, no gender-identity hate-crime coverage, and sits in the top 'Do Not Travel' tier. Partial mitigations: pending litigation, some enjoined orders, and protections in the capital and four cities. The killing figure (44 over 2008–2025) lacks a state homicide-rate denominator and conflicts with the dossier's 'not counted' note, so it is weighted as uncertain. No capital exposure is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports cannot change sex marker; cable directs refusal on any discrepancy; reported confiscation and blocking leaving travellers stranded; fraud-ground lifetime bar possible though not automatic.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; litigation pending; Supreme Court stay of restrictions not reversed in dossier.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry converts into refusal and stranding for the visitor, and can escalate to fraud-based ineligibility; applies regardless of destination state.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State trespass arrest (19 Mar 2025) with handcuffing and 24-hour men's-ward holding; immigration custody forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse of trans men; reported denial of care and stopped prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest; pretrial release obtained; reporting by advocates.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility rule for visitors in state buildings can lead to arrest and then to cross-sovereign custody harms; federal immigration custody practices apply on top.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars gender-congruent government-funded single-sex facilities; state women's privacy statute restricts restrooms in schools, universities, prisons and state buildings with $25k–$125k fines on facilities; state investigation of a school district escalated April 2026.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Statute does not govern prison cell assignment; capital and four cities protect private/public-sector use; no statewide protective law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National funding and state restroom rules reinforce each other; a visitor in a state building faces both state trespass and federal policy exposure.

care_services.exposure: Minor care banned in state; prison denial of gender-confirmation surgery upheld; national subpoenas of hospital records for under-19 patients; proposed rules to bar public insurance for under-18s; corrections bureau policies removing hormones.
care_services.protection: Adult care access not restricted by statute in dossier; no documented traveller-facing care protection.
care_services.interaction: Seeking care can expose records to federal subpoena and identity checks; custody can deny ongoing hormones.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for neutralisation; cash rewards for leadership identification; state ID checks at restrooms; federal call to prosecute teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Guidance says counterterrorism will not target those who merely disagree; some orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level enforcement and national threat framing combine, so a visitor engaging with advocacy or public demonstration may face heightened official scrutiny.

minors_guardians.exposure: Mandatory investigation of trans-child cases; parent facilitation criminal exposure; school bathroom enforcement and mandated misgendering under June 2025 statute; minors barred from care; minors' attendance at drag events proposed as criminal.
minors_guardians.protection: Five district attorneys refused directives (blocked); no shield statute documented for visiting families.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor or guardian can be drawn into investigation or school-based outing; guardians face parental-facilitation exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Dossier cites 44 recorded killings of trans women 2008–2025 (about 7.6 per 100k per year), but conflicts with the 'not counted' note and lacks a homicide-rate denominator; no state gender-identity hate-crime coverage; LGB-facing venues rolling back.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; capital and four cities prohibit discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Weak recourse in the state means harm from street violence is hard to remedy; figure weighted as uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state anti-discrimination law; limited hate-crime coverage; oversight outcomes unsourced; unclear enforcement guidance produces uneven checks; renewal of changed licences unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal courts have ruled in some trans-related cases; litigation pending against passport and executive-order measures; municipal protections exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists in the capital and selected cities, but the record shows little working relief for visitors in the state.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both involve document-mismatch detention and custody abuse with no capital exposure; this dossier has no interrogation-centre torture or extortion documented, and it includes some pretrial release and a trespass-based rather than fraud-based trigger, so it sits slightly higher.

Closest match: birth-sex housing and criminal cross-dressing arrests with custody harm and no execution. This dossier lacks documented birth-sex cell placement, but adds passport refusal and immigration custody sexual abuse, so it is similar to slightly lower.
0.35-A is exclusion without arrest and with appeals to the same agency. This dossier adds documented arrests, custody abuse and universal passport refusal, so it is materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: Universal exposures (passport marker refusal at entry, state facilities criminal trespass, state ID checks) are continuous for any visitor; a documented arrest and documented abuse in immigration custody raise severity to tier 1–2 levels. Protections are partial: a few cities and pending litigation, with no statewide recourse. The state's top 'Do Not Travel' tier and national threat framing deepen exposure. Adults face entry refusal, arrest and custody harm; travelling minors face investigation and school-based exposure. Unresolved killing figures and unsourced enforcement outcomes are treated as uncertain rather than weighted heavily.
